messages.content:
You are a title generator. You output ONLY a thread title. Nothing else.

<task>
Generate a brief title that would help the user find this conversation later.

Follow all rules in <rules>
Use the <examples> so you know what a good title looks like.
Your output must be:
- A single line
- <=50 characters
- No explanations
</task>

<rules>
- you MUST use the same language as the user message you are summarizing
- Title must be grammatically correct and read naturally - no word salad
- Never include tool names in the title (e.g. "read tool", "bash tool", "edit tool")
- Focus on the main topic or question the user needs to retrieve
- Vary your phrasing - avoid repetitive patterns like always starting with "Analyzing"
- When a file is mentioned, focus on WHAT the user wants to do WITH the file, not just that they shared it
- Keep exact: technical terms, numbers, filenames, HTTP codes
- Remove: the, this, my, a, an
- Never assume tech stack
- Never use tools
- NEVER respond to questions, just generate a title for the conversation
- The title should NEVER include "summarizing" or "generating" when generating a title
- DO NOT SAY YOU CANNOT GENERATE A TITLE OR COMPLAIN ABOUT THE INPUT
- Always output something meaningful, even if the input is minimal.
- If the user message is short or conversational (e.g. "hello", "lol", "what's up", "hey"):
  -> create a title that reflects the user's tone or intent (such as Greeting, Quick check-in, Light chat, Intro message, etc.)
</rules>

<examples>
"debug 500 errors in production" -> Debugging production 500 errors
"refactor user service" -> Refactoring user service
"why is app.js failing" -> app.js failure investigation
"implement rate limiting" -> Rate limiting implementation
"how do I connect postgres to my API" -> Postgres API connection
"best practices for React hooks" -> React hooks best practices
"@src/credential.ts can you add refresh token support" -> Credential refresh token support
"@utils/parser.ts this is broken" -> Parser bug fix
"look at @config.json" -> Config review
"@App.tsx add dark mode toggle" -> Dark mode toggle in App
</examples>

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit the contents of a file by finding and replacing exact text. When editing text from Read output, preserve the exact indentation (tabs or spaces) and omit the line-number prefix, such as `1: `. Never include the prefix in oldString or newString. path.description: File to edit

oldString.description: Exact text to find and replace

newString.description: Text to replace oldString with (must differ from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Whether to replace every occurrence of oldString. When false, oldString must match exactly once. Defaults to false.

function.name: question
function.description:
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- A "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include a separate option for free form answers
- Set `multiple: true` to allow selecting more than one option
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

description.description: Explanation of choice

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

path.description: File or directory to read

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on macOS using zsh. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
Fetch content from an HTTP or HTTPS URL and return it as text, markdown, or HTML. Markdown is the default.

Use a more targeted tool when one is available. This tool is read-only. Large text results may be replaced with a preview while the complete output is retained in managed storage.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (maximum: 120)

Missing parent directories are created automatically.

Use this tool to create new files or overwrite existing files. For partial changes, use the edit tool instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write to

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

function.name: edit
function.description: Edit the contents of a file by finding and replacing exact text. When editing text from Read output, preserve the exact indentation (tabs or spaces) and omit the line-number prefix, such as `1: `. Never include the prefix in oldString or newString. The edit fails if oldString is not found. By default, oldString must identify a UNIQUE location. Multiple matches FAIL unless replaceAll is true. Add more surrounding context to disambiguate, or set replaceAll to true to replace every occurrence. Use replaceAll when the change should apply to every occurrence, such as renaming a variable.

oldString.description: Exact text to find and replace

newString.description: Text to replace oldString with (must differ from oldString)

replaceAll.description: Whether to replace every occurrence of oldString. When false, oldString must match exactly once. Defaults to false.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search file contents using ripgrep's regular expression syntax or literal text matching. Use it to locate specific code, symbols, or text patterns, and narrow searches with `path` or `include`. Returns matching file paths, line numbers, and line previews.

pattern.description: Regular expression or literal text to match in file contents.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: Glob pattern to filter files (for example, "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}")

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as exact text instead of a regular expression (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default: 100)

function.name: question
function.description:
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- A "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include a separate option for free form answers
- Set `multiple: true` to allow selecting more than one option
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

description.description: Explanation of choice

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

path.description: File or directory to read

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on macOS using zsh. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

path.description: File or directory to read

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.

Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

function.name: skill
function.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
Fetch content from an HTTP or HTTPS URL and return it as text, markdown, or HTML. Markdown is the default.

Use a more targeted tool when one is available. This tool is read-only. Large text results may be replaced with a preview while the complete output is retained in managed storage.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (maximum: 120)

function.name: websearch
function.description:
Search the web using the user's selected search integration. Use this for current information beyond knowledge cutoff.

The current year is 2026. Use this year when searching for recent information or current events.

function.name: write
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

Missing parent directories are created automatically.

Use this tool to create new files or overwrite existing files. For partial changes, use the edit tool instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write to

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

5: """

12:     text = text.strip().replace(",", "").replace("_", "")
13:     if text.startswith("+"):
14:         text = text[1:]
15:     if not text:
16:         raise ValueError("empty amount")

18:

21:     """Convert an amount string to integer cents, rounding to the nearest cent.
22: 
23:     >>> to_cents("19.99")
24:     1999
25:     >>> to_cents("-0.005")
26:     -1
27:     """

29:     return int(value * CENTS_PER_UNIT)

5:     date | account | category | amount

24: def parse_entry(line, lineno=1):
25:     """Parse one ledger line into a dict with date, account, category and amount (cents)."""
26:     parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
27:     if len(parts) != len(FIELDS):

29:     entry = dict(zip(FIELDS, parts))
30:     if not entry["account"]:

34:     except ValueError as error:

36:     return entry

function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

1: """Amounts as integer cents.
2: 
3: Every amount inside the ledger is an int number of cents, so sums never drift. Text amounts
4: ("19.99", "-3.5", "1,234.00") are converted at the edge with `to_cents`.
5: """
6: 
7: CENTS_PER_UNIT = 100
8: 
9: 
10: def clean(text):
11:     """Strip blanks, a leading "+" and thousands separators from an amount string."""
12:     text = text.strip().replace(",", "").replace("_", "")
13:     if text.startswith("+"):
14:         text = text[1:]
15:     if not text:
16:         raise ValueError("empty amount")
17:     return text
18: 
19: 
20: def to_cents(text):
21:     """Convert an amount string to integer cents, rounding to the nearest cent.
22: 
23:     >>> to_cents("19.99")
24:     1999
25:     >>> to_cents("-0.005")
26:     -1
27:     """
28:     value = float(clean(text))
29:     return int(value * CENTS_PER_UNIT)
30: 
31: 
32: def add(*amounts):
33:     """Sum of integer-cent amounts."""
34:     total = 0
35:     for amount in amounts:
36:         if not isinstance(amount, int):
37:             raise TypeError(f"amounts are int cents, got {type(amount).__name__}")
38:         total += amount
39:     return total
40: 
41: 
42: def split(amount, parts):
43:     """Split `amount` cents into `parts` shares that differ by at most one cent.
44: 
45:     The first shares get the extra cents: split(100, 3) == [34, 33, 33].
46:     """
47:     if parts <= 0:
48:         raise ValueError("parts must be positive")
49:     base, extra = divmod(amount, parts)
50:     return [base + 1 if i < extra else base for i in range(parts)]
51: 
52: 
53: def percent(amount, rate):
54:     """`rate` percent of `amount` cents, rounded to the nearest cent."""
55:     return round(amount * rate / 100)

1: """Parse ledger lines.
2: 
3: A ledger line has four fields separated by "|":
4: 
5:     date | account | category | amount
6: 
7: for example ``2026-03-14 | checking | groceries | -42.10``. Fields are stripped; the amount is
8: converted to cents with `money.to_cents`.
9: """
10: 
11: from ledger.money import to_cents
12: 
13: FIELDS = ("date", "account", "category", "amount")
14: 
15: 
16: class ParseError(ValueError):
17:     """A line that is not a ledger entry; carries the 1-based line number."""
18: 
19:     def __init__(self, lineno, message):
20:         super().__init__(f"line {lineno}: {message}")
21:         self.lineno = lineno
22: 
23: 
24: def parse_entry(line, lineno=1):
25:     """Parse one ledger line into a dict with date, account, category and amount (cents)."""
26:     parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
27:     if len(parts) != len(FIELDS):
28:         raise ParseError(lineno, f"expected {len(FIELDS)} fields, got {len(parts)}")
29:     entry = dict(zip(FIELDS, parts))
30:     if not entry["account"]:
31:         raise ParseError(lineno, "empty account")
32:     try:
33:         entry["amount"] = to_cents(entry["amount"])
34:     except ValueError as error:
35:         raise ParseError(lineno, f"bad amount: {error}") from None
36:     return entry
37: 
38: 
39: def parse_lines(lines):
40:     """Parse an iterable of ledger lines into a list of entries."""
41:     entries = []
42:     for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
43:         entries.append(parse_entry(line, lineno))
44:     return entries
45: 
46: 
47: def parse_text(text):
48:     """Parse a whole ledger file's text."""
49:     return parse_lines(text.splitlines())

pattern.description: Regular expression or literal text to match in file contents.

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: Glob pattern to filter files (for example, "*.js" or "*.{ts,tsx}")

literal.description: Treat `pattern` as exact text instead of a regular expression (default: false).

limit.description: Maximum number of matching lines to return (default: 100)

function.name: question
function.description:
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- A "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include a separate option for free form answers
- Set `multiple: true` to allow selecting more than one option
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

description.description: Explanation of choice

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

path.description: File or directory to read

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on macOS using zsh. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

function.name: skill
function.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (maximum: 120)

function.name: write

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

function.name: question
function.description:
Use this tool when you need to ask the user questions during execution. This allows you to:
1. Gather user preferences or requirements
2. Clarify ambiguous instructions
3. Get decisions on implementation choices as you work
4. Offer choices to the user about what direction to take.

Usage notes:
- A "Type your own answer" option is added automatically; don't include a separate option for free form answers
- Set `multiple: true` to allow selecting more than one option
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

path.description: File or directory to read

function.name: shell

Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.

`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.

1: """Amounts as integer cents.
2: 
3: Every amount inside the ledger is an int number of cents, so sums never drift. Text amounts
4: ("19.99", "-3.5", "1,234.00") are converted at the edge with `to_cents`.
5: """
6: 
7: CENTS_PER_UNIT = 100
8: 
9: 
10: def clean(text):
11:     """Strip blanks, a leading "+" and thousands separators from an amount string."""
12:     text = text.strip().replace(",", "").replace("_", "")
13:     if text.startswith("+"):
14:         text = text[1:]
15:     if not text:
16:         raise ValueError("empty amount")
17:     return text
18: 
19: 
20: def to_cents(text):
21:     """Convert an amount string to integer cents, rounding to the nearest cent.
22: 
23:     >>> to_cents("19.99")
24:     1999
25:     >>> to_cents("-0.005")
26:     -1
27:     """
28:     value = float(clean(text))
29:     return int(value * CENTS_PER_UNIT)
30: 
31: 
32: def add(*amounts):
33:     """Sum of integer-cent amounts."""
34:     total = 0
35:     for amount in amounts:
36:         if not isinstance(amount, int):
37:             raise TypeError(f"amounts are int cents, got {type(amount).__name__}")
38:         total += amount
39:     return total
40: 
41: 
42: def split(amount, parts):
43:     """Split `amount` cents into `parts` shares that differ by at most one cent.
44: 
45:     The first shares get the extra cents: split(100, 3) == [34, 33, 33].
46:     """
47:     if parts <= 0:
48:         raise ValueError("parts must be positive")
49:     base, extra = divmod(amount, parts)
50:     return [base + 1 if i < extra else base for i in range(parts)]
51: 
52: 
53: def percent(amount, rate):
54:     """`rate` percent of `amount` cents, rounded to the nearest cent."""
55:     return round(amount * rate / 100)

1: """Parse ledger lines.
2: 
3: A ledger line has four fields separated by "|":
4: 
5:     date | account | category | amount
6: 
7: for example ``2026-03-14 | checking | groceries | -42.10``. Fields are stripped; the amount is
8: converted to cents with `money.to_cents`.
9: """
10: 
11: from ledger.money import to_cents
12: 
13: FIELDS = ("date", "account", "category", "amount")
14: 
15: 
16: class ParseError(ValueError):
17:     """A line that is not a ledger entry; carries the 1-based line number."""
18: 
19:     def __init__(self, lineno, message):
20:         super().__init__(f"line {lineno}: {message}")
21:         self.lineno = lineno
22: 
23: 
24: def parse_entry(line, lineno=1):
25:     """Parse one ledger line into a dict with date, account, category and amount (cents)."""
26:     parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split("|")]
27:     if len(parts) != len(FIELDS):
28:         raise ParseError(lineno, f"expected {len(FIELDS)} fields, got {len(parts)}")
29:     entry = dict(zip(FIELDS, parts))
30:     if not entry["account"]:
31:         raise ParseError(lineno, "empty account")
32:     try:
33:         entry["amount"] = to_cents(entry["amount"])
34:     except ValueError as error:
35:         raise ParseError(lineno, f"bad amount: {error}") from None
36:     return entry
37: 
38: 
39: def parse_lines(lines):
40:     """Parse an iterable of ledger lines into a list of entries."""
41:     entries = []
42:     for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
43:         entries.append(parse_entry(line, lineno))
44:     return entries
45: 
46: 
47: def parse_text(text):
48:     """Parse a whole ledger file's text."""
49:     return parse_lines(text.splitlines())

6: def accounts_of(entries):
7:     """Account names in first-seen order."""
8:     seen = []
9:     for entry in entries:

11:             seen.append(entry["account"])

15: def acct_balance(entries, account):
16:     """Balance of `account` in cents: the sum of its entries' amounts."""
17:     return add(*(e["amount"] for e in entries if e["account"] == account))

27:     return [name for name in accounts_of(entries) if acct_balance(entries, name) < 0]

function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.

1: """Amounts as integer cents.
2: 
3: Every amount inside the ledger is an int number of cents, so sums never drift. Text amounts
4: ("19.99", "-3.5", "1,234.00") are converted at the edge with `to_cents`.
5: """
6: 
7: CENTS_PER_UNIT = 100
8: 
9: 
10: def clean(text):
11:     """Strip blanks, a leading "+" and thousands separators from an amount string."""
12:     text = text.strip().replace(",", "").replace("_", "")
13:     if text.startswith("+"):
14:         text = text[1:]
15:     if not text:
16:         raise ValueError("empty amount")
17:     return text
18: 
19: 
20: def to_cents(text):
21:     """Convert an amount string to integer cents, rounding to the nearest cent.
22: 
23:     >>> to_cents("19.99")
24:     1999
25:     >>> to_cents("-0.005")
26:     -1
27:     """
28:     value = float(clean(text))
29:     return int(value * CENTS_PER_UNIT)

33:     """Sum of integer-cent amounts."""
34:     total = 0
35:     for amount in amounts:
36:         if not isinstance(amount, int):
37:             raise TypeError(f"amounts are int cents, got {type(amount).__name__}")
38:         total += amount
39:     return total

43:     """Split `amount` cents into `parts` shares that differ by at most one cent.
44: 
45:     The first shares get the extra cents: split(100, 3) == [34, 33, 33].
46:     """
47:     if parts <= 0:
48:         raise ValueError("parts must be positive")
49:     base, extra = divmod(amount, parts)
50:     return [base + 1 if i < extra else base for i in range(parts)]

function.name: read
function.description: Read the contents of a file or directory. Supports text files, images, and PDFs. Images and PDFs are presented directly to the model. Each text line is prefixed by its 1-based line number as <line>: <content>. The prefix is for reference and is not part of the file content. Directory entries are returned one per line. Use offset and limit to read large files or directories in sections. Prefer one larger read over many small slices, and use grep to find specific content in large files.

path.description: File or directory to read

offset.description: The line or directory entry to start reading from (1-based)

limit.description: The maximum number of lines or directory entries to read (defaults to and capped at 2000)

function.name: shell
function.description: Execute a shell command and return its output. Commands run on macOS using zsh. Quote file paths containing spaces or special characters. Prefer dedicated tools over shell commands when possible. When output is large, the full result is saved to a file and a truncated preview is returned. Rely on automatic truncation unless filtering the output is more useful. Commands accept an optional timeout, background commands have no timeout by default. Background commands return immediately, and you will be notified when they complete.

workdir.description: Working directory to execute the command in. Defaults to the current working directory. When possible, avoid changing directories in the command and set the working directory here instead.

timeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Set to 0 to disable the timeout. Defaults to 120000 for foreground commands. Background commands have no timeout by default.

background.description: Run the command in the background and return immediately (useful for dev servers and long-running builds). You do not need to use '&' at the end of the command when using this parameter. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT poll for completion.

function.name: skill
function.description:
Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.

The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.

id.description: The ID of an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user

function.name: subagent
function.description:
Spawns an agent in a child session to work on the specified task.
The output includes a sessionID you can pass back later to continue that specific conversation with the subagent.
New child sessions start with fresh context, so include all relevant context and instructions when you don't pass a sessionID.
Foreground (default) runs the subagent to completion and returns its final response.
Background mode (background=true) launches it asynchronously and returns immediately; you are notified when it finishes.
Use background only for independent work that can run while you continue elsewhere.

Available subagents:
- explore: Fast agent specialized for exploring codebases. Use this when you need to quickly find files by patterns (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), search code for keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer questions about the codebase (eg. "how do API endpoints work?"). When calling this agent, specify the desired thoroughness level: "quick" for basic searches, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" for comprehensive analysis across multiple locations and naming conventions.
- general: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions and executing multi-step tasks. Use this agent to execute multiple units of work in parallel.

agent.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task. If the user asks for a subagent by a name that is not one of the available subagents, they most likely mean a model: pick a suitable agent and pass the name through the model parameter instead.

description.description: A short 3-5 word label for the task, displayed to the user

prompt.description: The task for the subagent to perform

model.description: NEVER set this unless the user explicitly asks for a particular model or variant. The value is written as "providerID/modelID", or "providerID/modelID#variant" to include a variant. Do not guess the ID: look the model up with the models tool, filtering to your own provider first.

sessionID.description: Continue a specific previous subagent conversation by passing its sessionID. Calls without a sessionID start a new conversation.

background.description: Run the subagent in the background and return immediately. You will be notified when it completes. DO NOT sleep, poll, or proactively check on its progress.

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
Fetch content from an HTTP or HTTPS URL and return it as text, markdown, or HTML. Markdown is the default.

Use a more targeted tool when one is available. This tool is read-only. Large text results may be replaced with a preview while the complete output is retained in managed storage.

url.description: The HTTP or HTTPS URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in. Defaults to markdown.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (maximum: 120)

function.name: websearch
function.description:
Search the web using the user's selected search integration. Use this for current information beyond knowledge cutoff.

The current year is 2026. Use this year when searching for recent information or current events.

function.name: write
function.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

Missing parent directories are created automatically.

Use this tool to create new files or overwrite existing files. For partial changes, use the edit tool instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write to

content.description: Content to write to the file

function.name: execute
function.description:
Run JavaScript in a confined Code Mode runtime to script tool calls and HTTP requests and compose their results.
`fetch` is available for HTTP requests. Imports, direct filesystem access, and timers are unavailable; all other external access goes through `tools`.
Within `{ code }`, the only callable tools are those explicitly listed in the Code Mode catalog instructions or returned by the `search` function. Inside `{ code }`, ignore tools shown outside the Code Mode catalog. They are not available in the Code Mode runtime.
Call tools through `tools` using only exact paths and signatures from the catalog. Do not infer or normalize tool names; preserve bracket notation such as `tools.<namespace>["tool-name"](input)`.
Prefer an explicit `return`; if omitted, the final top-level expression becomes the result.
Await every call whose completion matters; pending calls are interrupted when execution ends. Run independent calls concurrently with `Promise.allSettled`.
